Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.3 Mass, Volume, Weight and Density (8 Lessons) By the end of the 
Topic 3.4: Time, Distance and Speed
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, Distance and Speed, part of Measurements 3.3 Mass, Volume, Weight and Density (8 Lessons) By the end of the  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we observe speed in daily activities? 2. Why does time vary in different places of the world?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Engage in purposive groups/pairs activities that will involve measuring distances and time, for example running track events to determine speed. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to measure distances and time. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Engage in purposive groups/pairs activities that will involve measuring distances and time, for example running track events to determine speed. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to measure distances and time. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time, Distance and Speed together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy – as the learner participates in track events to measure speed.

● Digital literacy -as the learner uses IT devices to determine time in different zones in the world.

● Citizenship- global citizenship as the learner determines local time in different parts of the world.

36

Values:
● Integrity- as the learner correctly records individual running time during track events and other games.

● Respect - as the learner adheres to their lanes on track events and other games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Safety - as the learner observes safety measures and time during games and sports.

● Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) - as the learner participates and chooses careers in games and sporting

activities.

● Self-awareness - as the learner participates and times themselves in games.

Link to other subjects:

Integrated Science - as the learner uses digital devices to tell time in different zones of the world.
